title: CANFAR · Usage
description: Cumulative resource consumption per user, community and session kind over a fixed window. Retrospective accounting, not a live view — for what is running now see Platform Overview, and for capacity being held but not used see Efficiency & Waste. The window is chosen by the variable, not the time picker, which is hidden because it does not apply.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Data source
list.description: Metrics backend the panels query. Seeded at install time.

list.name: window
list.label: Window
list.description: How far back to accumulate. This replaces the time picker, which is hidden. All time is bounded by how long the backend retains these series.

list.name: scrape
list.label: Scrape interval (s)
list.description: Sampling interval of the container metrics, used to integrate the gauge-based figures into hours. CPU is counter-based and unaffected. Set this wrong and memory, GPU and session-hours scale by exactly the wrong factor, so it is visible rather than buried.

panels.title: Totals for the selected window
panels.description: Everything on this dashboard is cumulative over the window chosen above, not a reading of what is running now. There is no time picker: the window is the only time control.

panels.title: CPU core-hours
panels.description: Total CPU actually consumed, from the container CPU counter, so this is measured usage rather than what was requested. Exact: a counter needs no sampling assumption.

targets.expr:
sum(
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) / 3600

panels.title: Memory GiB-hours
panels.description: Working set integrated over the window. Memory has no counter, so this is a Riemann sum of the gauge multiplied by the scrape interval; a step with no sample contributes zero, which is correct because the session did not exist.

targets.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600 / 1024^3

panels.title: GPU-hours
panels.description: GPU time held, from the nvidia.com/gpu resource request. This is allocation, not utilisation — a held GPU may be idle. Real utilisation needs a DCGM exporter, which is not deployed.

targets.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="nvidia_com_gpu"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600

panels.title: Session-hours
panels.description: Total wall-clock time sessions spent Running, summed across sessions.

targets.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"$namespace", phase="Running"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600

panels.title: Sessions launched
panels.description: Distinct sessions seen in the window, counted by session id, so a session that restarted is still one session.

targets.expr: count(count by (label_canfar_net_id) (max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])))

panels.title: By user
panels.description: Ranked highest first. Capped to the top 25 so one busy period cannot render thousands of bars.

panels.title: CPU core-hours by user
panels.description: CPU core-hours consumed per user over the window, largest first. Ranked highest first and capped at the top 25; on a busy window far more users than that will have usage, so read this as the leaderboard rather than the whole population.

targets.expr:
topk(25,
sum by (label_canfar_net_username) (
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  * on (namespace, pod) group_left (label_canfar_net_username) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) / 3600

> 0
)

panels.title: By community
panels.description: Two attributions side by side because they disagree today. `canfar.net/community` is the label Skaha writes and is the one to steer by long term, but every session currently launches with `default`, so it renders a single bar. Kueue's ClusterQueue is the dimension that actually carries a split right now.

panels.title: CPU core-hours by community
panels.description: CPU core-hours per community, largest first. A single `default` bar means attribution is not being set at launch, not that the dimension is unused.

targets.expr:
topk(25,
sum by (label_canfar_net_community) (
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  * on (namespace, pod) group_left (label_canfar_net_community) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!="", label_canfar_net_community!=""}[$window])
) / 3600

> 0
)

panels.title: CPU core-hours by ClusterQueue
panels.description: CPU core-hours per ClusterQueue, largest first. Kueue adds this label to the pod at admission; it is not written by Skaha.

targets.expr:
topk(25,
sum by (label_kueue_x_k8s_io_cluster_queue_name) (
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  * on (namespace, pod) group_left (label_kueue_x_k8s_io_cluster_queue_name) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!="", label_kueue_x_k8s_io_cluster_queue_name!=""}[$window])
) / 3600

> 0
)

panels.title: By session kind
panels.description: The same four measures split by session type, which is the dimension that usually explains a change in the other two.

panels.title: CPU core-hours by session kind
panels.description: CPU core-hours per session kind over the window, largest first.

targets.expr:

) / 3600
> 0

panels.title: CPU core-hours wasted
panels.description: Requested CPU integrated over the window, minus what was actually consumed. Computed from the request gauge and the usage counter directly rather than from an average, so an idle period counts as idle instead of being skipped.

targets.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="cpu"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600
-
sum(
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) / 3600

panels.title: Memory GiB-hours wasted
panels.description: Requested memory integrated over the window, minus the working set actually held.

targets.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="memory"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600 / 1024^3
-
sum(
  sum_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600 / 1024^3

panels.title: Mean session length
panels.description: Session-hours divided by distinct sessions launched. A platform of many short sessions behaves very differently from one of few long ones, and the two totals beside this cannot show which you have.

targets.expr:
(
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"$namespace", phase="Running"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600
)
/ (count(count by (label_canfar_net_id) (max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window]))) > 0) * 3600

panels.title: Efficiency over the window
panels.description: What fraction of the resource reserved for sessions was actually used. This is the ratio the totals above and the waste figures below imply but never state. Low is bad here, so unlike the volume counters these are coloured.

panels.title: CPU efficiency
panels.description: CPU consumed divided by CPU requested, over the window. Sessions reserve cores at launch and are charged for them whether or not they burn them; this says how much of that reservation did any work.

targets.expr:
(
sum(
  increase(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) / 3600
)
/ (
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="cpu"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600
> 0)

panels.title: Memory efficiency
panels.description: Working set held divided by memory requested, over the window. Lower than CPU efficiency usually means sessions are sized for a peak they rarely reach.

targets.expr:
(
sum(
  sum_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", container!="", container!="POD"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600 / 1024^3
)
/ (
sum(
  sum_over_time(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="memory"}[$window])
  and on (namespace, pod) max_over_time(kube_pod_labels{namespace=~"$namespace", label_canfar_net_username!=""}[$window])
) * $scrape / 3600 / 1024^3
> 0)
